title: From the Editor — Already Waiting
settingText: Hushwater: a weathered house at the edge of the road with winter damage still visible in repairs and pale wood. Through an open doorway, a small sealed packet rests on a plain table in the foreground. No readable label, no character reveal.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 12. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Raina planted identities. Samuel planted expectations. Together they created encounters that looked impossible until somebody showed you the wires.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then the impossible kept happening outside the trick.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now they have traveled together long enough that nobody can have run ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No quiet conversations. No planted names. No careful setup.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A house there has been holding something since winter for a man Brandon Mack has never been.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This time, everyone arrives at the mystery together.

title: The House That Was Waiting
summary: At Hushwater, Maela Crow recognizes Brandon as Andrew Keane and produces a sealed packet she has been holding for Andrew. Because Raina and Samuel have remained with the group since the Long Mile, neither could have primed Hushwater during the current approach; the older provenance still has to be established.

panelPlan.text: Hushwater is a modest settlement of shaded houses and a communal dining court, with no obvious Sunforge in the immediate center.
Maela sees Brandon, says 'Andrew Keane' with tired relief rather than shock, and goes inside before he can correct her.
Maela returns with a visibly old sealed cloth packet marked for ANDREW KEANE: faded fabric, worn folds and an old tied seal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That's a long time to wait for the wrong man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Who told you he was coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Woman passing through. Green scarf. Shaved on the left side.

title: The Promise in the Packet
summary: Maela explains that a dying friend asked her to hold the packet for Andrew Keane and that a later traveler described Brandon's appearance closely enough that she believed the promise finally had an endpoint.

panelPlan.text: Maela brings out Lysa's sealed packet and sets it on the table between herself and Brandon without placing it in his hands.
She explains that her friend Lysa died believing Andrew would come. Months later another traveler gave a description matching Brandon.
Brandon leaves both hands away from the packet while Maela's frustration shows in her face and grip on the table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: And that isn't all. Lysa gave me this for Andrew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Do you? The traveler described your face, your coat, even the way you stand near a door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Because his name is on it.

title: Before Raina
summary: Raina reconstructs the dates from Maela's household ledger. The ledger records the later traveler who described a man matching Brandon and linked him to Andrew; that visit predates Raina first learning Brandon's name and predates Samuel joining her. The explanation exposed in Issue 4 cannot have caused this setup.

panelPlan.text: Raina lays her dated notes beside Maela's household ledger. Keep both dates and the handwritten ANDREW entry legible enough to compare while the group leans over the table.
Samuel asks for the traveler's description. Maela remembers a woman with a shaved left temple and a green scarf, nobody Samuel recognizes.
Eva watches Raina try every ordinary explanation before finally accepting the chronology.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: And the date is on this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Could the Last Drop story have doubled back?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I've checked the date three times. The Last Drop hadn't happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I remember because I was furious about something unrelated that same day.

title: We Know Him
summary: Eva and Jessie no longer reopen the possibility that Brandon is secretly Andrew. Their months of ordinary life with him have made the identity question emotionally obsolete even while the external mystery deepens.

panelPlan.text: After exhausting chronology, Raina admits there is one remaining human explanation she dislikes: Brandon might actually have known Andrew. Outside Maela's house, Eva, Jessie, Raina and Samuel argue over provenance while Brandon sits apart mending a strap.
Raina asks whether they can truly exclude Brandon having some unknown connection to Andrew. Eva answers before Brandon does.
Jessie stands beside Eva and answers Raina without consulting the notes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: There's still a chance Brandon knew Andrew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. I don't think that's what this is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: You don't know every year of his life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Knowing him now doesn't close the missing years.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It changes what I'm willing to believe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He can surprise us. He probably will. But he's Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Then Andrew is the interesting part.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I preferred being the boring part.

title: What the Promise Belongs To
summary: Brandon helps Maela separate her promise to Lysa from the mistaken belief that he is Andrew. Maela decides to keep the packet rather than force closure through the wrong man.

panelPlan.text: Maela keeps the packet in both hands as she tells Brandon she wanted him to be Andrew; her posture is tired rather than accusatory.
Brandon tells her he cannot release her, but that keeping a promise does not require pretending the wrong person fulfilled it.
Samuel watches Brandon do pastoral work without naming it and understands why communities keep making use of him even when the assigned identity is false.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I wish you were. I wanted you to be him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Then I could be finished with this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Lysa died believing he'd come. I promised her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: So what am I supposed to do with it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: The preacher would have something better.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I am trying very hard not to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I only know I'm not Andrew. If you open it for me, you're still giving it to the wrong man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: So I still have to decide.

title: The Question Moves
summary: The group leaves Hushwater with the first arc's human conspiracy definitively demoted from cause to interference. Eva states the new question: not who Brandon is, but why people and stories keep arriving before him.

panelPlan.text: After Brandon accepts Maela's mild dislike as fair, Eva offers the only closure she can: she has crossed out an old question. Maela remains at her doorway with the sealed packet, choosing not to manufacture closure.
The five travelers move out together in one loose group, with Raina and Samuel walking alongside the rig rather than separated ahead or behind.
On the road, Eva closes the old page in her notebook labeled WHO IS BRANDON? and starts a new one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Then what are you chasing now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why do strangers keep expecting someone with Brandon's face before we arrive?

title: Sunforge Outlaw Will Return
settingText: An immense western Sunfields road vanishing into luminous distance. Tiny travelers move forward while, on a remote ridge far off the road, a single unreadable rider silhouette may or may not be the same figure seen before. No supernatural effects.
summary: Art-directed season-closing editorial splash. Close the first twelve-issue movement while propelling the larger mystery forward without resolving it.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Brandon Mack is still Brandon Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The road ahead is not getting simpler.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Somewhere beyond Hushwater are towns they have never seen, people with stories that should not be there yet, and a Rider who has already taught them not to trust distance.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Enough to know the first answer was only interference.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The road has stopped asking who Brandon is.
